translation_notes: prefixes: BEING->being, PM->pm, PROVENANCE->provenance, YURTLE->yurtle -- all four verified as real `Namespace(...)` bindings in yurtle_rdflib/namespaces.py at the pinned commit, not guessed. `from .namespaces import BEING, PM, PROVENANCE, YURTLE` -> `from yurtle_context import being:, pm:, provenance:, yurtle:` (dynamic regime, the construction under test: the import, not ns_def_local -- no @prefix line with an inlined IRI). All four are imported (mirroring the real file's own import list) even though only PROVENANCE is dereferenced inside this specific region's body; kept as prefixes anyway because they ARE namespace objects genuinely imported by the real line, same convention as the ns_import_project sibling for this repository (YurtleStore._flush_file).

`if p == PROVENANCE.definedIn:` -> `if p == provenance:definedIn:` -- a prefixed name used directly as a term in a comparison, immediately followed by the if-statement's own trailing colon; transpiles cleanly and the fixture-corruption check below confirms it is not silently ignored.

`filtered.add((s, p, o))` -> `+{ {s} {p} {o} }(filtered)`, the call-suffix form: no ambient `@graph` is declared (the function receives/produces graphs by parameter and return value, not a module-level graph), so the island names its receiver graph explicitly, per current-graph.md's `+{ }(other)` example -- same pattern as the ns_import_project sibling (YurtleStore._flush_file) in this same repository.

`for s, p, o in self.store:` (a full, unconstrained 3-variable scan) is left as plain Python iteration rather than rewritten to `m{ ?s ?p ?o }(self.store)`: no idiom in INSTRUCTIONS.md SS2's correspondence table covers an unconstrained full-store scan, and turning it into a BGP with zero fixed terms buys nothing over the native rdflib iterator -- unlike the `trav_navigation`-style fixed-subject case in the sibling region, where `m{ }` genuinely lets a fixed term replace a filter. The `self.store.namespaces()` iteration a few lines above is likewise left untouched: it walks namespace *bindings*, not triples, and no construction in the closed vocabulary covers that.

Executability (AGENT_BATCH's 163-regions case): the region is a method body (`self.store`, set by `super().__init__(store)` in rdflib's own `Serializer` base class, serializer.py line 65) with no visible graph in its own three lines of context, so a minimal `FakeSerializer` (only the `.store` attribute this region's body reads) plus a `demo()` harness are appended identically to original.py and translated.ldpy. `.namespaces` rewritten to `yurtle_context`, a shim module transcribing the four real `Namespace(...)` objects verbatim from yurtle_rdflib/namespaces.py (ldpy's `from … import p:` reads them under the prefixes' upper-cased names).

Fixture designed to isolate the two independent filters in the region (provenance predicate vs. file:// object) so a break in either shows up on its own: the PROVENANCE.definedIn triple carries a non-file literal object (would slip through the file:// filter alone), the file:// triple carries an ordinary predicate (would slip through the predicate filter alone), plus one ordinary kept triple and one kept triple with a namespace-term object. Checked directly: replacing the predicate guard with `if False: continue` first passed unnoticed with an earlier fixture where the provenance triple's object also happened to be a file:// URI (the second filter masked the first) -- fixed by giving that triple a non-file object; re-broken afterward with `if False: continue` and confirmed `rdfeval check` now FAILs (2 vs 3 triples), then reverted and reconfirmed OK.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the two `if ...: continue` guards become one positive condition around the add (De Morgan), and str(o).startswith becomes o.startswith, o being a URIRef (a str) once the isinstance test has passed. The namespace-binding copy loop stays: assigning the store's namespace_manager would share it, not copy it. A `filtered += [...]` comprehension measures the same and would leave no place for an island, so the loop was kept.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `provenance:definedIn` in the comparison and `+{ {s} {p} {o} }(filtered)` with the call suffix (no @graph, which would bind the imported prefixes on the filtered graph). The demo() harness is copied from each side unchanged.
The notation gains nothing here: `+{ {s} {p} {o} }(filtered)` and `filtered.add((s, p, o))` weigh the same, as do `provenance:definedIn` and `PROVENANCE.definedIn`.
header_optimization_notes: Nothing unused in the header on either side: Graph, URIRef, Literal and the four namespaces (or prefixes) are all read by the region or by the demo() harness. optimized_header.py and optimized_header.ldpy are copies of the optimized artefacts.
